segments.t: rhetoric that's coming out of the administration that you're going to be responsible if you
make a mistake.
Everyone's kind of reassessing.
You can have these spectacular earnings, spectacular revenues, dreams, great projections.
But if all of a sudden we wake up one day and a model has gone rogue, or a bad actor
has used it maliciously and you've got a doughnut, it makes...
But you've been warning about that issue for a long time.
We've had you on the broadcast where I remember we started a conversation.
We were starting to go one way and then all of a sudden you said, no, no, no, I just was
at an AI conference and the people there genuinely...
You may have been one of the first people who said that on our air in terms of this sort
of true risk.
How big a risk actually is in your mind?
We run three quant teams internally and then I have another business, Sports Analytics.
We've been using neural nets forever, AI, forms of AI forever, and again, the difficulty
with it is that you know what the output is, but you don't know why or how you got there.
That's what happens when you have billions and trillions of permutations.
You don't know why we got there.
And so that's why AI safety's always been a concern for me because interpretability,
generates that outcome.
If you don't know how or why it happens, it's got to be a great concern.
